summary: New entry `/autopilot` lets the user arm a bounded grant before an absence. While it is active the orchestrating session presents no question. It classifies a question by every effect of its recommended option: when every class it touches is allowed, it records the decision with `autopilot.py record` first, then applies it and writes it where the flow records the user's answer, marked with the grant id; any never effect, any excluded effect the grant does not allow, and doubt queue the question with `autopilot.py queue` while the work that does not depend on it continues. Under `owner_gates` at `two_fixed_gates` the grant is the owner's advance answer for its allowed classes, and every queued question is also a `pending` row of the Delivery's `User Decisions` table. Classes, goal kinds and durations are data in `skill-content/autopilot/data/autopilot-policy.json`: `choice`, `approval_gate` and `merge` are allowed by default, `release` and `phase_start` are excluded by default, and `credentials`, `security_settings`, `spending`, `destructive` and `scope_or_rule` are never delegated. A grant ends at a time (`--for` or `--until`, default 8 h, at most 72 h), at a goal the owning compiler reads as terminal (`delivery:DLV-###` merged or cancelled, `requirement:REQ-###` incorporated, resolved with no change, superseded or withdrawn, `text:` only through `complete`), at its cap (48 h by default), or through `off` and `complete`. Only the user arms a grant: each host's user-prompt hook records the typed `on` command as a short-lived arming record, `on` refuses without it and takes the options only from it, and a pre-tool hook denies the host question tool while a grant is active. The guard stops an agent that runs the packaged script, not a process that writes the runtime files with the user's filesystem authority; `vault_hook.py` narrows that gap by denying tool writes into `.agentrof/agent-marketplace/.runtime/autopilot/` and putting back what a shell command adds to the grant or the arming record there. A grant governs only the session, on the host, whose user typed it, so a parallel session of either host asks as usual. A built package that cannot show its arming hook fails closed, and a grant armed under another guard, longer than the maximum or holding a never class is inactive. `off`, `status` and `report` list the decisions of every grant a re-armed grant replaced, and an unreadable grant file is moved aside so the next grant can start. The grant is private, ignored runtime state; with no grant every compiler output and task binding is unchanged. `tools/validate.py` rejects a duplicate class or goal kind, an unknown default, an empty never set, a default above the maximum and a readable goal kind without terminal statuses.
